headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy to propose tariffs that shift the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and distribution infrastructure to large energy users, such as data centers, rather than residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer groups, Clean Virginia, Senator L. Louise Lucas, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Dominion Energy (with amendments).
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Legislation Shifting Data Center Energy Costs.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, aiming to prevent residential customers from subsidizing data center development. This bill, HB 1393, requires Dominion Energy to propose tariffs that allocate capacity procurement and distribution infrastructure costs to large energy users, specifically those with 25 MW or greater demand.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities to report the total volume of water supplied to data centers to the Department of Environmental Quality, enhancing transparency on their water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Public Data Center Water Usage.
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality, making this information publicly accessible. This transparency measure aims to address concerns about data centers' significant water consumption and will be aggregated on the DEQ website.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to evaluate sound profiles and potential impacts on water, agriculture, parks, and historic sites before local approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents, Delegate Josh Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Virginia Adds New Restrictions on Data Center Siting and Noise.
news_summary: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills, including HB 153, that introduce new siting requirements for large data centers. This legislation mandates impact assessments on noise, water, agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval, addressing community concerns about data center development.
